land.text: the Lordship of Schellenberg and the County of Vaduz, bought from the Hohenems in 1699 and 1712

predecessors.note: The two estates were bought by the House of Liechtenstein before the principality existed; Cliopatria keeps its small imperial estates inside the 'Holy Roman Empire Minor States' aggregate. 23 January 1719 is the decree that united them.

capitals.name: Vaduz
capitals.note: 'Its capital is Vaduz.' Neither page opened dates Vaduz as the seat from 1719; the History page does not call it the capital.

rulers.name: Anton Florian
rulers.note: Reigned from 12 March 1718 to 11 October 1721 (page); only the years from the principality's founding in 1719 are shown.

rulers.name: Joseph Wenzel I
rulers.note: Second reign (the first, 16 June 1712 to 12 March 1718, is before the principality): 22 December 1748 to 10 February 1772.

rulers.name: Hans-Adam II
rulers.note: From 13 November 1989; the page lists him as incumbent. Hereditary Prince Alois has been 'Hereditary Prince and Regent' since 15 August 2004 (page).

correction.text: the 1721 shape (Vaduz and Schellenberg) given to 1719-1720: 'On 23 January 1719 ... Charles VI ... decreed that Vaduz and Schellenberg were united'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Liechtenstein shape begins in 1721, but the page dates the principality to 23 January 1719. The lands (Schellenberg bought 1699, Vaduz 1712) are the same as the 1721 shape.

The History page: 'Liechtenstein's borders have remained unchanged since 1434, when the Rhine established the border', so no change of shape between 1719 and 1949.

'Liechtenstein's borders have remained unchanged since 1434'; the only later change on the page is the 1949 cession of the Ellhorn mountain to Switzerland, below the grid's resolution. region.text: the Lordship of Schellenberg and the County of Vaduz, united and raised to a principality

ledger.note: 1719: Charles VI raises Vaduz and Schellenberg to the Principality of Liechtenstein. 'On 23 January 1719, after the lands had been purchased, Charles VI, Holy Roman Emperor, decreed that Vaduz and Schellenberg were united' and elevated them to a Reichsfürstentum, named for Anton Florian of Liechtenstein; 'Liechtenstein became a mostly-sovereign immediate member state of the Holy Roman Empire.' The History page: Schellenberg was bought in 1699 and Vaduz in 1712 (the Liechtenstein page names the buyer Hans-Adam I, the History page Johann Adam Andreas).

region.text: France invaded the country on 6 March 1799

ledger.note: March 1799: France occupies Liechtenstein in the War of the Second Coalition. 'France invaded the country on 6 March 1799' and plundered several towns, Nendeln among them (the page names no other town); 18,000 French troops under Masséna were stationed in the country. The principality stays Liechtenstein's; only control is lost.

region.text: the Austrian and Vorarlberg state militias liberated the country by 14 May

ledger.note: May 1799: Austrian and Vorarlberg militias under Jelacic defeat the French and liberate the country 'by 14 May'. The page gives no day for the first fighting; month 5 is the page's own.

region.text: the Ellhorn mountain, ceded to Switzerland

ledger.note: 1949: Liechtenstein cedes the Ellhorn to Switzerland. 'In 1949, Liechtenstein ceded the Ellhorn mountain to Switzerland as a result of Swiss demands...' The only territorial change on the page; far below the grid's resolution. Dates on the page: Balzers refused in November 1948 and the Landtag approved the transfer 'the following month'; no day is given for the cession, so the event stays at year 1949.

wars.name: War of the Second Coalition

zones.text: the whole country, invaded by France on 6 March 1799 and liberated by 14 May

wars.outcome: France occupied all of Liechtenstein from 6 March 1799; Austrian and Vorarlberg militias defeated the French and liberated it by 14 May 1799. No change of territory.
wars.note: Only the 1799 invasion of Liechtenstein is read from the page (the full span of the war is not on it). Liechtenstein itself did not field an army; the Habsburg side is the Austrian and Vorarlberg militias under Jelacic. Recorded as occupation_start/occupation_end (hatched), not contest events: France held the whole country for about ten weeks, and the fighting that ended it is a single liberation, not a front that moved. Added after review of 2026-10-25.

wars.name: Napoleonic Wars
wars.outcome: After Austerlitz (1805) and the end of the Empire, Liechtenstein became a sovereign state in 1806 by joining Napoleon's Confederation of the Rhine; the page notes that Maximilian I of Bavaria wanted to annex it in 1806, which did not happen. No change of territory.
wars.note: Considered and kept with no zones: Liechtenstein is not named as a fighting party. Membership of the Confederation of the Rhine: 'From 25 July 1806 ... the Prince of Liechtenstein was a member, in fact a vassal, of its hegemon' (Liechtenstein page; its infobox gives 12 July 1806); the confederation was dissolved 'on 19 October 1813'.

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War
wars.outcome: Prince Johann II placed soldiers at the German Confederation's disposal 'only to defend the German territory of Tyrol'; the Liechtenstein army marched home on 22 July after the war; the Confederation was dissolved in 1866 and Liechtenstein became fully independent. No change of territory.
wars.note: Outside Cliopatria's years; listed so the war is seen to have been considered. The Liechtenstein page gives the Confederation as 20 June 1815 to 23 August 1866, the History page to 24 August 1866.

certainty.note: The History page: 'Liechtenstein's borders have remained unchanged since 1434, when the Rhine established the border'; the page names no survey or treaty, but the state is a fixed administrative unit of 160 km2 whose only recorded change is the 1949 cession of the Ellhorn.

notes: START: Cliopatria's row begins 1721; the page dates the principality to 23 January 1719 (new keyframe 1719-1720, same shape). Schellenberg (1699) and Vaduz (1712) were bought before it existed and are described in the found event, not as gains. END: Cliopatria's row stops in 1814 (data/polities.csv has no other row for Q347) but the state exists today; the dossier therefore runs to 2024, the end year other living states use, with no dissolve event, and a new keyframe 1815-2024 repeats the 1814 shape. The orchestrator can trim it if the modern-era group is to own Liechtenstein; no such dossier was checked. STATUS WITHOUT TERRITORY: member of the Confederation of the Rhine from 25 July 1806 (the page says 'in fact a vassal' of Napoleon, the infobox 12 July 1806) to its dissolution on 19 October 1813; member of the German Confederation from 20 June 1815 to 1866. The vassal tint belongs in the suzerain's dossier (first-french-empire or a Confederation of the Rhine dossier), as vassal_start/vassal_end with counterpart principality-of-liechtenstein (Cliopatria's Confederation of the Rhine row runs only 1809-1814, three years after the 1806 founding); this dossier carries no vassal event because the grammar puts it on the suzerain's side. German Confederation membership (1815-1866) is the german-confederation row's to record. FIXED AFTER REVIEW (2026-10-25): the French occupation of 1799 (invaded 6 March, liberated by 14 May) is now an occupation_start/occupation_end pair against french-directory and a War of the Second Coalition entry, all from the History page; the ruler strip (twelve princes, 1719-2024) is read from List of monarchs of Liechtenstein, a third page opened on the reviewer's suggestion, one over the 1-2 page budget. NOT FOUND ON THE PAGES: the date Vaduz became the seat (the History page does not call it the capital), the day of the 1949 cession (the page: Balzers refused in November 1948, the Landtag approved 'the following month'). Three pages used (budget 1-2). GAZETTEER NAMES NEEDED: Ellhorn (a peak on the Liechtenstein-Switzerland border; the pages do not say in which commune). COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: none new; confederation-of-the-rhine and german-confederation are Cliopatria rows owned by other groups.
